summary: A Codex wake stopped by a second top-level thread keeps its old delivery facts, so it reports and records 'receipted' (or 'declared') forever while it will never announce mail again.
failure_scenario: Pinned wake sends a notice, its receipt lands (facts: last_push_at set, oldest_unreceipted_at None). A second top-level thread calls the same server -> observe() sets stopped=True but leaves facts and _dirty untouched. Every later lane-qualified send to this server's lanes gets recipient_delivery='receipted' from the push_delivery row (delivery.states_for), and list_agents().you.delivery says 'receipted', yet poll() returns None forever: the sender is told the wake works while nothing will ever wake the thread.
evidence: Read observe() (codex_queue.py:311-316), Announcer.poll/state and delivery.states_for. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hardline-mcp/8cf8860e-b349-5ae5-be4c-c6f46cd42c01/scratchpad/probe1.py: after receipt then a second top-level thread, wake.stopped=True, wake.state()='receipted', delivery.states_for(own identity)='receipted', and still 'receipted' a day later on the injected clock. docs/codex-queue-wake.md:168 says only that a stopped wake sends nothing; no doc or test covers what it reports.

summary: A channel push that carries only notices (a pointer to a name held before, or 'this session now holds X') is recorded as an unreceipted push but its text never asks for the receipt, so delivery degrades to 'unreceipted' after the grace with nothing broken.
failure_scenario: A reconnected conversation has mail waiting at a name it held before and none at its own lanes. next_batch() returns notice-only params (ids=[]); run() calls sent([], nonce, built), which appends to unreceipted and sets oldest_unreceipted_at. The content is only channel.pointer(lane): the 'Read with ... receipt=...' line is appended only `if due`. The model has no instruction to echo the nonce (it is only in meta), so after GRACE (10 min) state()/the push_delivery row read 'unreceipted' until some later mail push happens to be receipted. CLAUDE.md tells the session to fall back to a Monitor on 'unreceipted', and senders see recipient_delivery='unreceipted' for a working channel. The inbox wake (announce) does not have this problem: its constant notice always asks for the receipt.
evidence: Read Pusher.next_batch/sent/run. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hardline-mcp/8cf8860e-b349-5ae5-be4c-c6f46cd42c01/scratchpad/probe1.py with waiting_before stubbed to one old lane and no owned lanes: ids=[], 'receipt=' not in content, and state() 11 minutes later on the injected clock = 'unreceipted'. tests/test_hints.py::test_a_push_names_the_lane_once_and_never_shows_the_mail asserts the content equals channel.pointer(OLD) exactly, i.e. pins the receipt-less text, and never calls sent()/state().

summary: address() accepts the socket if ANY of up to six ancestors' session records names it, not the nearest Claude session's, so the very case the docstring cites (a nested session that binds no inbox passing an outer one's variables on) still wakes the outer session - a stranger's turn.
failure_scenario: Outer interactive session A (pid 30) binds S_outer and writes sessions/30.json naming it. Inside it a nested Claude session B that binds no inbox (the docstring's --bare case) launches hardline; hardline inherits CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET=S_outer. The walk hardline -> B -> shell -> A finds no match at B (no record, or a record without messagingSocketPath) and continues to A, whose record names S_outer == env -> Inbox(S_outer). Every hardline notice for B's lanes is posted into A's inbox, starting turns in A. The doc table (claude-inbox-wake.md:20) claims 'the nearest claude.exe ancestor', but the code never stops at the first Claude session or rejects a match beyond one; test_an_inbox_no_ancestor_records_is_not_used models only a two-process chain whose one record names another socket, so the outer ancestor is never in the walk.
evidence: Read address()/_names and procid.ancestry_snapshot (no stop at a session). Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hardline-mcp/8cf8860e-b349-5ae5-be4c-c6f46cd42c01/scratchpad/probe2.py with chain [hardline 10, node 20, bash 25, node 30] and only 30.json naming the env socket: address() returns Inbox(outer) both with no 20.json and with a 20.json lacking messagingSocketPath. The premise that a no-inbox session passes the outer variables on is the module's own docstring and docs/claude-inbox-wake.md:59-60; whether Claude Code --bare writes a session record at all was not checked, but either way the walk reaches the outer record.

summary: Nothing tests that prune() keeps a row whose liveness is UNKNOWN: changing `== DEAD` to `!= ALIVE` (delete on uncertainty, against CLAUDE.md's 'deletion requires certainty') passes the whole suite.
failure_scenario: A regression that deletes push_delivery/codex_routes rows for processes whose probe returned UNKNOWN (e.g. access denied on Windows for another user's or elevated process) would silently drop a live server's facts, turning its recipients' recipient_delivery into 'unknown' and its not_top_level mark into nothing - and no test would fail.
evidence: Scratch mutation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hardline-mcp/8cf8860e-b349-5ae5-be4c-c6f46cd42c01/scratchpad/muts.py, cases2.json 'prune-unknown'): delivery.py `instance_state(r[0], r[1]) == DEAD]` -> `!= 'alive']`; full suite `python -m pytest tests -n 4`: 1318 passed, 20 skipped. The only prune test (tests/test_codex_route_facts.py::test_routes_of_a_dead_process_are_pruned) stubs only DEAD and ALIVE.

summary: Any error reply to turn/start clears the duplicate-submission cooldown, including -32603, which codex_steer documents as an error Codex can return after a submission landed.
failure_scenario: turn/start is admitted, then the app-server answers with an internal error (-32603). _rpc sets uncertain_until=0.0 ('a matching rejection proves this submission did not run'), so the next poll with mail still pending starts a second turn for the same notice. codex_steer.NOT_ADMITTED deliberately excludes -32603 for exactly this reason (tests/test_codex_steer.py:122 'steer_turn's own failure maps to -32603 after the submission landed'); wake_codex makes the opposite assumption about the same server.
evidence: Read _rpc and poll; compared with codex_steer.NOT_ADMITTED and its test. Not demonstrated: I did not confirm that Codex's turn/start handler can return -32603 after starting a turn; the inconsistency between the two modules' assumptions is what is shown. tests/test_wake_codex.py::test_definite_turn_rejection_leaves_no_submission_uncertainty uses -32602 only.

summary: The refusal test parametrizes over codex_steer.NOT_ADMITTED itself, so removing a code from the implementation removes its test case instead of failing it.
failure_scenario: Dropping -32001 (overloaded) from NOT_ADMITTED turns an overloaded daemon's refusal into Ambiguous: the notice stays outstanding and is retried after 300 s instead of being queued at once. The suite still passes (one fewer parametrized case).
evidence: Scratch mutation 'steer-overloaded-ambiguous' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hardline-mcp/8cf8860e-b349-5ae5-be4c-c6f46cd42c01/scratchpad/cases1.json): codex_steer.py NOT_ADMITTED without -32001 -> slice tests 216 passed (217 before; the -32001 case vanished). Same root cause would hide removal of any other code.

summary: The 'only a sweep that started at the front may forget' guard (`start == 0`) is untested in both announce.poll and Pusher.next_batch (channel.py:296).
failure_scenario: With the guard removed, a poll that resumed mid-backlog (>10,000 unread) and reached the end drops every announced id below the cursor from `announced` (re-announcing old deferred mail, against 'deferred mail is not re-announced'), and the pusher deletes their reminder schedule (re-pushing them at once). No test fails.
evidence: Scratch mutations 'fullsweep-forget-any' (announce.py) and 'pusher-fullsweep-any' (channel.py), `start == 0 and self._cursor == 0` -> `self._cursor == 0`: full suite 1318 passed, 20 skipped for each. test_a_backlog_beyond_one_polls_scan_is_swept_across_polls does not observe this.

summary: The version check that keeps an older fact snapshot from overwriting a newer one in Pusher._write is untested.
failure_scenario: Removing `if version <= self._written: return` lets a push recorded on the pusher thread and a receipt on a tool thread write out of order, leaving the stored row 'awaiting/unreceipted' after a receipt (or the reverse); the suite still passes.
evidence: Scratch mutation 'pusher-write-order': full suite 1318 passed, 20 skipped.

summary: announce.Announcer gate: reservation before send, take_back only on NotSent of an initial send, resends never revalidated (documented), receipt resets backoff; 10 scratch mutations of poll/_dispatch/take_back/accept_receipt/unsettled all killed by tests/test_announce_batch.py, test_unsettled_notices.py, test_hints.py, test_claude_inbox.py.

announce._dispatch revalidation re-reads exact reserved ids in chunks of 500 and rechecks grant and stop under the lock before sending; any read failure raises NotSent so the batch is rolled back rather than treated as empty.

claude_inbox.post/send: connect failure is NotSent, short or failed write after connect is maybe-delivered, a still-blocked late writer is never joined by a second, and a late success only settles the same notice text; each guard killed by a scratch mutation.

codex_steer outcome mapping: handshake/initialize failures are Unreached, anything after the steer frame starts is Ambiguous, only an int code in NOT_ADMITTED is a refusal (bool/list codes rejected), fragmented frames reassembled, replies matched by id; mutations of each killed.

codex_queue.CodexWake.send: Ambiguous steer raises without queueing, one retry only for a changed turn, a queue failure is never NotSent; observe pins only a top-level thread and only the pinned thread's calls set the turn; mutations killed (observe-stop-subagent by tests/test_thread_names.py).

delivery: record/record_routes column counts match ROUTE_KEYS; prune is CAS on (pid, process_key); _read takes one snapshot for both tables and push facts outrank the not_top_level mark (mutation killed by tests/test_subagent_lanes.py).

wake_codex.CodexWake: cooldown reserved before turn/start, empty snapshot clears uncertainty, mail rechecked after status, endpoint restricted to loopback ws without path/credentials, version floor enforced; mutations killed by tests/test_wake_codex.py.
Baseline: the 8 slice test modules (217 tests) pass at 2296778 on Linux; the full suite passes in a scratch copy (1318 passed, 20 skipped, all skips are opt-in live/platform marks).
